history.summary: Entry-ticket 3BR (872 sqft, $2.568M / $2,945 psf) in a 212-unit low-rise 99LH estate in a D10 GCB pocket, 0.7-1.0 km from King Albert Park DTL, TOP mid-2030. Priced at parity with Skye at Holland's launch and ~3% over completed Fourth Avenue Residences on a harmonised basis, for a location weaker than both on transit and amenities. Yield ~3.0%, no income until 2030, and 2,270+ new 99LH units in the same belt TOP into the 2029-32 exit window. Fair as a family home; does not work as a 4-7 yr resale-profit trade.
history.rating_rationale: Value: not cheap. On the same 3BR band and harmonised basis the guide psf is +2.9% over completed FAR ($2,862 eq., MRT at the door, realsmart REALSCORE 2.1 / +1.3%/yr), +1.2% over Skye at Holland's launch ($2,910, Holland Village MRT), and -2.5% under Dunearn House C1 ($3,021, Sixth Ave MRT 4 min) — a ~6% discount to FAR's age-adjusted new-build equivalent, which is what the 1 km MRT walk and empty precinct cost. Region: CCR, the worst realized forward region (+1.9%/yr) and the nearest 99LH comps confirm it (FAR +1.3%/yr, OHVR +2.2%/yr, Van Holland's only resale -6.5%/yr). Exit math at the guide: bear -$167k, base +$81k (+0.6%/yr, below T-bills), bull +$337k (+2.4%/yr); break-even needs $3,055 psf at yr 5. Carry: ~3.0% gross (< 3.5% fallback), zero income for 3.8 yrs. Liquidity: 3BR-only entry at $2.57M, above the $2.2M knee and 99% of her ceiling; the exit buyer is a family/right-sizer, not an investor, and 2,270+ fresher 99LH units (Skye, Dunearn House x2, Holland Plain plots 2-3) land in the same window. Bull case (first mover under a land-price umbrella: plot 2 $1,491 vs $1,432 psf ppr; CRL interchange 2032; 74-unit 3BR scarcity; GCB-enclave product) is real but a one-time step of ~4% land uplift, thinner than Dunearn House's 15%. Buy trigger: <=$2.45M ($2,810 psf) acceptable, <=$2.40M ($2,750) good — neither is a launch-day price. 4BR from $3.175M and 5BR from $3.992M: out of envelope and above the $3M liquidity knee — Avoid for this mandate. Mandate exception: NOT justified — fails region, yield, quantum and ceiling rules simultaneously and beats neither Dunearn House C1 nor completed FAR decisively.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: No rentals exist (uncompleted). URA 2025-26 3BR 900-1,000 sqft contracts: Fourth Ave $6,850 (n=16, MRT-door), Royalgreen $6,475 (n=10), Hyll $5,950 (n=14). $6,500/mo for 872 sqft liveable at a 1 km walk -> ~3.0% gross at $2.568M; expat-family tenant on housing allowance is the pool, and 2,000+ new units in the belt will cap rents 2030-33. Below the 3.5% fallback line.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Use CCR realized +1.9%/yr as the base, not the developer story. Bear: exit at today's completed-comp level ($2,860) = -$167k. Base $3,150 (+1.4%/yr on entry) = +$81k, under T-bills. Bull $3,450 needs Holland Plain plots 2-3 launching at $3,200-3,400 AND the precinct maturing by 2031-32 = +$337k / +2.4%/yr. The 0-5 yr cohort is the worst forward-return cohort (amortising launch premium) and this exits at age 1-3.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No per-stack facing data in text sources (profile saved with stacks: []). Physical priors: 11 blocks of 4-6 storeys on a corner plot — take the TOP floor (5 or 6) of any stack, since low-rise offers no other vertical premium; prefer stacks facing Holland Green Linear Park / GCB interior over Holland Plain road frontage; avoid the boundary shared with Sim Lian's plot 2 (~280 units, construction 2027-2031, permanent view change) — confirm which side at the showflat stack selector; check west exposure on the selector (no source states orientation). Luxe (private lift) stacks are 4BR Premium/5BR only — irrelevant to the 3BR mandate.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: CCR full-panel realized forward baseline; realsmart FAR +1.3%/yr and OHVR +2.2%/yr avg annualised resale profit
agent_evaluation.mandate_exception_call: NO. Out of mandate (CCR) and fails four crash rules at once: region, yield (3.0% < 3.5%), quantum ($2.568M > $2.2M), ceiling ($2.568M = 99% of $2.59M). It is not cheaper than Dunearn House C1 by enough (-2.5% psf on the same 872 sqft) to trade a 4-min MRT walk for a 1 km one, and completed FAR at ~$2.82M earns 3.4% from day one at an MRT door. An exception would need <=$2.40M on a top-floor park-facing stack — not a launch-day outcome.

history.summary: 4BR from $3.175M / $2,921 psf (1,087 sqft) up to 4BR Premium $3.674M / 1,227 sqft with private lift. Cheapest psf in the project and the right family format for the GCB pocket, but $3.2M+ is outside both buyer envelopes and above the $3M exit-liquidity knee.
history.rating_rationale: Out of envelope ($3.175M vs $2.59M) — cannot be bought without a gift-flex beyond $2.6M plus a larger loan than TDSR allows, and it breaches the never-at-the-ceiling rule outright. On merit it is the best-priced type (psf below the 3BR, 74-unit cohort, Luxe private-lift variants) and the natural product for landed right-sizers, but the resale buyer for a $3.3-3.9M 99LH 4BR 1 km from MRT is thin, CCR forward is +1.9%/yr and yield ~3.2%. If the owner ever widened the envelope, this type beats the 3BR on relative value; it still does not beat the mandate.
